subject: Spatial modeling of AADT on norwegian traffic road network

messages.author: a8ff1dce8cf96214
messages.subject: Spatial modeling of AADT on norwegian traffic road network
parts:
Hi,

I have a dataset where each row is a directed traffic link on the Norwegian road network, together with a sparse adjacency matrix showcasing the structure. 

The column "aadt" in the dataset is the response variable, where around 15% are not None. It looks like the data follows a negative binomial distribution: 
mean      4337.405121
std       6535.791136
min          1.000000
25%        732.000000
50%       2016.000000
75%       5248.000000
max      52998.000000

The adjacency matrix looks like this: 

adj_matrix_df
    row   col data             row_id             col_id
1     1 21236    1 1017091719-AGAINST    1017091718-WITH
2     1 30443    1 1017091719-AGAINST    1017091719-WITH
3     1 43305    1 1017091719-AGAINST 1017580067-AGAINST
4     2  2710    1    1017162113-WITH    1017162090-WITH
5     2 20967    1    1017162113-WITH    1017162115-WITH

and the dataset has a column called id which is used as an identifier. It is also sorted so that it has the same order(row_index 4 is the same id as row 4 in the dataset).

I am currently setting up the graph like this: 
"""
graph <- sparseMatrix(i = adj_matrix_df$row,
                      j = adj_matrix_df$col,
                      x = adj_matrix_df$data)

# Calculate row sums excluding diagonal
row_sums_excluding_diagonal = rowSums(graph) - diag(graph)

# Set non-diagonal elements to -1
graph[graph != 0 & !diag(graph)] <- -1

# Set the diagonal elements of the precision matrix
# Adding a small constant to ensure the matrix is positive definite
diag(graph) <- row_sums_excluding_diagonal + 1e-6

data$link = 1:num_links
 """
And then 
"""
formula <- aadt ~ f(link, model = "besag",graph=graph, prior = "mvnorm", scale.model = TRUE) + "the covariates appear here"

result <- inla(formula, family = "nbinomial", data = data,
               control.predictor=list(link=1))
"""

I am wondering if this is a valid approach?

The results I get are okay, but I am wondering if they can be improved. I understand this is a hard question to answer right off the bat, so I am mostly wondering if the graph is setup correctly, and if the setup of the formula and INLA are correct.

Ha en fin dag, hilsen tidligere fysmatter.

- Johannes

I just wonder if you would like to use this package

that defines proper models _on_ road networks which can also be used by
INLA.

Let me know if this is not what you want.

All the best
